newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-Atlantic power jumps on gas, cold, outage.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-Atlantic power jumps on gas, cold, outage.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the Mid-Atlantic U.S. jumped Thursday on continued strength in the natural gas market, a cold snap due to arrive overnight and outage of a major nuclear generating unit.
"It's primarily on the cold and the screen," said a Houston marketer, referring to the arrival of the weather system that put the Midwest in a deep freeze and a rally in NYMEX gas futures.

Firm, peak PJM electricity for Friday soared more than $10 to $42.00-$44.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) from Wednesday's $30.00-$33.00. A number of next-day deals for firm, peak delivery were heard done in the $40.00-$44.00 range.
Firm, off-peak PJM power for Friday was assessed at $14.00-$17.00, up from Wednesday's $13.00-$14.00.
Friday's temperatures in the midsection of the eastern seaboard were predicted to range in teens to 30s Fahrenheit degrees, down from today's 30-50 range.

NYMEX January Henry Hub natgas futures were last up 25.0 cents per million British thermal units at $4.330. Swing gas prices at the Philadelphia city gate were quoted in the $5.30-$5.50 range, up about 50 cents from Wednesday.

The 1,055 megawatt (MW) Limerick 2 nuclear generating unit in Pottsdam, Pa., was taken off line late Wednesday to repair a leaking seal. The power unit was planned to return to operation over the weekend.
A 600 MW unit at the coal-fired Homer City, Pa., power station, which was shut Monday due to a oil feed pump problem, was expected to resume service Friday.
There were also talks of reduced output, less than 100 MW at one of two 850 MW units the Keystone coal-fired plant near Johnstown, Pa., this week, according to market sources.

Some participants were also trying to scheduled power into regions west of the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect district because the lingering steep chill and talk of unplanned plant outages there, market sources said.
January/February 1997 PJM power deliveries were pegged at $31.50-$32.00, up from $31.25-$31.40 Wednesday with late morning deals heard done today at $31.50-$31.90.
March PJM deliveries rose to $25.25-$25.90, up from Wednesday's $25.00-$25.50.
First-quarter 1997 PJM was notationally assessed at $29.50-$30.00, up from $29.20-$29.50 Wednesday.
July/August 1997 PJM power was assessed at $31.90-$32.15, down from Wednesday's $32.35.
Third-quarter 1997 PJM held at $29.00-$29.25, and fourth-quarter 1997 PJM remained at $24.00-$24.50.
Calendar 1997 for peak hour delivery in PJM was steady at $26.40-$26.70.
